headline: Agentic boom lifts output, power prices and anger; states tax compute to cope

events: Spring capability jump: long-horizon coding and back-office agents run multi-day tasks with minimal supervision; enterprise adoption doubles to ~24% of firms
Big Tech AI capex passes $700bn annualised; US data-centre grid interconnection queues exceed 300 GW and PJM/ERCOT capacity prices hit records
Insurers, banks and BPO firms announce hiring freezes; Philippine and Indian call-centre employment starts falling
Fed holds at ~3.5% as goods disinflation from AI offsets electricity and services inflation; world growth 3.4%
US-China agree a limited tariff truce extension; chip export controls stay but trade volumes stabilise
Second jump: agentic systems handle most routine legal, accounting, claims and customer-service workflows; US white-collar unemployment for under-30 graduates reaches 11%
Electricity price spike (US retail power +18% y/y, gas-turbine shortage) pushes G20 inflation to 4.6%; ECB and Fed pause cuts, 10y Treasury touches 5.4%
Q3 AI-equity correction of ~30% after a hyperscaler cuts capex guidance; recovers within 9 months as agent revenues show up
US election dominated by 'robots and rates'; populist winner promises an automation levy and data-centre power caps
Displaced clerical workers and drivers stage mass protests in France, South Korea and India; first robotaxi depots torched in two US cities
Global unemployment peaks at 6.9%; measured US productivity growth runs above 3% for a second year
US passes a 'Compute Dividend Act': a per-kWh levy on large AI data centres funding wage insurance and retraining credits; EU adopts a similar digital-labour tax
China rolls out state-directed 'AI+ industry' push with humanoid robots in factories, tightening youth job market but boosting exports to the Global South
Nuclear restarts, SMR orders and record solar-plus-storage build, much of it financed by AI firms, ease power prices in the second half
Pakistan, Egypt and Kenya enter IMF-led restructurings as BPO and remittance income falls and Treasury yields stay high
Border clashes in the Horn of Africa escalate into an Ethiopia-Eritrea war
Third jump: AI-driven drug discovery and materials design produce first approved AI-designed medicines and a battery chemistry breakthrough announcement
Inflation falls back to ~2.5% as AI deflation in services dominates; central banks cut to ~3%, easing debt rollover
Japan briefly faces a JGB auction failure; BoJ steps in with yield caps, fuelling yen weakness
OECD countries trial shorter working weeks and job-guarantee pilots; Spain and Canada introduce partial basic-income payments
Bangladesh suffers sovereign distress as garment automation and US/EU nearshoring hit exports
Firms using AI in production reach ~61%; agent 'workforces' outnumber human employees at several large banks and insurers
Unemployment eases to 6.2% as care, construction, energy and in-person services absorb workers, but at lower median wages
Top 10 AI and energy firms account for nearly half of S&P 500 market cap; wealth concentration at record highs
Data centres consume ~6% of global electricity; renewables reach 44% of power but gas burn also higher, warming 1.58C
Trust in institutions near multi-decade lows; anti-AI parties enter governments in two EU states

winners: Frontier AI labs, hyperscalers and chipmakers
Utilities, grid equipment, nuclear and storage builders
Owners of capital and high-skill AI-complementary professionals
Skilled trades and in-person care workers in tight labour markets
losers: Routine white-collar workers and recent graduates in rich countries
Highly indebted sovereigns facing high real rates (Japan, frontier markets)
bullets: World growth averaged ~3.6% as AI lifted productivity, but gains flowed mainly to capital and a narrow set of firms and regions.
About 140 million jobs were displaced cumulatively; re-employment came mostly in lower-paid physical and care work, so inequality rose sharply.
Power became the binding constraint: a 2028 electricity-driven inflation spike delayed rate cuts and turned data-centre siting into a political battlefield.
Governments responded with compute and automation levies, wage insurance and partial basic-income pilots, but public debt still crept up to ~99% of world GDP.
Trade tensions plateaued rather than escalated; AI services and chips became the main arena of US-China rivalry.
The Global South split: AI-enabled exporters (Vietnam, Mexico, Gulf) gained while BPO and garment economies faced debt distress and four sovereign crises.
Social unrest and anti-AI populism rose markedly, with trust in institutions falling to ~33/100.
Clean energy accelerated thanks to AI-firm financing, yet surging demand kept emissions roughly flat and warming reached ~1.58C.
wildcard: In 2029 an autonomous trading-agent cascade triggered a 40-minute 'flash freeze' in US Treasury markets, forcing the Fed to backstop dealers and leading to mandatory AI-agent circuit breakers.
image_description: In a dim suburban kitchen, a former insurance adjuster in a plumbing-apprentice uniform checks her wage-insurance payment on her phone while the electricity meter glows red and a delivery robot hums past the window toward the floodlit data centre on the hill.
